no_book_tree: Further Exercises 2(a–h): no complete phrase-marker answers printed.
Further Exercises 3(a–b) and 4(a–c): prompts only; do not infer functions or trees.
book_flags: Every subordinate clause introduced by that, whether, or a subordinating conjunction is S-bar → C + S; omitted that is stored as an elided word in C.
After, until, before, and temporal since are prepositions taking S directly as complement (not S-bar).
Clausal subject/direct object is dominated by NP; subject-predicative S-bar is directly in VP; extraposed subject S-bar is a daughter of the main S.
Clause complements of A and N are sisters of the head A or N; whether-clause complements of P sit under PP as S-bar.
ACA triangles are numbered S1 (main), S2, etc.; include complementizers within subordinate clause triangles. The stored ACA uses numbered S indices and an explicit bracketed representation.
A clause contains one lexical verb; ACA validator checks the clause count against the explicitly transcribed clause list and preserves the book’s main-clause designation.
review_notes: Exercise 2(a): the exercise prompt and the answer diagram show “good film”; one extracted answer line reads “excellent film”. The diagram and prompt were preferred; note retained.
Exercise 2(c): prompt has “has ascended”; answer bracket text says “had ascended”. The diagram/page image and answer text conflict; note retained; tree follows the bracket text in nested chunk.
The initial [1b] is intentionally stored as printed with a bare S2; the chapter later generalises to S-bar + C for subordinate clauses.
Discussion 6 has a note/alternative for the Chapter 7 Appendix refinement of the modifying AP.
